clue.text: Stolen goods including ring, unknown to rascal

indicators.note: the word for stolen goods holds the other two pieces within it

parts.note: swag is slang for loot or stolen goods
to ring someone is to call them
Y is a mathematical unknown, as in x and y

explanation.surface: A thief's haul includes a ring, and the rascal knows nothing of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like jewellery among the loot, but it means telephone; 'including' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a mischievous rogue, a synonym for a rascal.

clue.text: Edge or border round lake

indicators.note: the word for border goes round the single letter for lake

parts.note: a side is a border or edge of something
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bank or shoreline running round a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edge' here is the verb: to edge along is to move sideways cautiously.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge forward and to sidle both mean to move sideways or furtively.

clue.text: Drug cut throughout and all get sick

indicators.note: every word in the phrase that follows is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A drug was adulterated, and everyone who took it fell ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut throughout' docks each word: AND, ALL, GET, SICK lose D, L, T, K to leave AN AL GE SIC. 'Cut' looks like the drug dealer's adulteration.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is a painkilling medicine, a kind of drug.

clue.text: One who takes people's words at their face value

definitions.text: One who takes people's words at their face value

parts.words: One who takes people's words at their face value
parts.note: taking words at face value usually means believing them, but here the words are literally read from the speaker's face, from the movement of the mouth

explanation.surface: A trusting soul who never doubts what anyone says.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person who reads mouth movements literally gets speech from someone's face.

clue.text: Hint to tie up one's estate in part of the West Indies

parts.note: wind is a hint or rumour, as in getting wind of something

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for tie is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game, a draw
one's taken as one is, I plus IS
an estate is landed property, lands

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone should put their property into a trust in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the tie word, since this is a down clue. 'tie up one's estate' reads as a legal phrase about trusts but splits into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windward Islands are a group in the Lesser Antilles, one region of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Crew tucked into yellow fish — ready to retire

indicators.note: the crew word is slipped inside the two-word yellow fish

parts.note: golden is a yellow colour
a hake is a fish of the cod family
the hands are the crew of a ship

explanation.surface: Sailors settle into a meal of yellow fish before going ashore for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ready' is a noun here: readies or ready money, cash given to someone leaving a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden handshake is a large payment made to an executive on retirement or departure, money for leaving.

clue.text: Protest by bishop producing reduction in forces

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or demonstration
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop leads a protest that leads to cuts in the armed services.
explanation.walkthrough: DEMOB is short for demobilisation, the British word for discharging troops after a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Demobilisation is the standing down of military personnel, a cut in troop numbers.

clue.text: Padre ordered to arrange a hanging

indicators.note: the padre is told to rearrange himself, so the letters of that word are shuffled

explanation.surface: A chaplain is instructed to organise an execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hanging' sounds grim beside a padre, but it is a curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a curtain or piece of hanging fabric.

clue.text: Fruit bat seen to circle

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Fruit bat seen to circle' (5), answer MANGO: no parse of 'bat seen to circle' gives MANGO without a word doing two jobs or an unsupported synonym; no blog or database found.

clue.text: Sleeping partner fled below at sea

indicators.note: being at sea is being confused, so the letters of fled below are jumbled

explanation.surface: A partner ran away underneath, out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleeping partner' suggests a silent business investor, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is someone who shares a bed, literally a sleeping companion.

clue.text: Still god remains inscrutable

parts.note: dead means motionless or still
Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A silent god stays impossible to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' is a link word, though it looks like corpses next to 'Still'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face is expressionless and gives nothing away, impossible to read.

clue.text: Intellectual found out

definitions.meaning: discovered or came to know, the past tense of a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Learned is scholarly as an adjective, and a past form of the verb meaning to discover.

clue.text: A bore is keen to be heard

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for keen gives a soundalike

parts.note: eager means keen

explanation.surface: A tedious person is anxious to get a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' looks like a dull person; it is a tidal wave running up a river, as on the Severn.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal surge up an estuary, the same thing as a river bore.

clue.text: We implore individual to include nothing miserable

indicators.note: the word we takes the nothing letter inside it

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
to implore is to beg
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: We beg someone to take in a miserable nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' makes the opening word of the clue the container, holding the zero-shaped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Woebegone describes someone looking sad and dejected, a synonym for miserable.

clue.text: Worthless diamonds put in post

parts.note: base metal is of low value, so base means worthless
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Cheap gems sent off in the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' is a station or position, not mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who is based somewhere is stationed there, assigned to that position.

clue.text: Space for the provision of meals in company's meeting-place

indicators.note: room for board puts the space after the meals in the answer

parts.note: board is meals provided, as in bed and board
room is space

explanation.surface: Somewhere to serve meals inside the firm's conference area.
explanation.definitionFit: A boardroom is where a company's directors hold their meetings.

clue.text: A learner tries again to start a practice session

indicators.note: the word for tries again comes first, at the start of the answer

parts.note: in law, to rehear a case is to try it again
L is the learner abbreviation, from the L-plate on a learner's car

explanation.surface: A novice has another go at kicking off a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tries again' is legal: courts rehear cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run before a performance.

clue.text: Attacker in trouble, grabbed by disguised SAS soldier, perhaps

indicators.note: the trouble word is seized and held inside the other letters
a disguise changes appearance, so the letters of SAS are rearranged

parts.note: a soldier is one kind of ant
to ail is to trouble, as in what ails you

explanation.surface: A gunman in difficulties is caught by an undercover special forces soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguised' shuffles the three-letter regiment and 'grabbed by' signals the container. The SAS is Britain's Special Air Service, a special forces regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who attacks another person.

clue.text: Son with three-wheeler not allowed to set off

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a trike is a tricycle
out means not permitted, as an idea ruled out

explanation.surface: A boy on a tricycle is forbidden to begin the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' looks like begin a journey; it means start out decisively.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike out is to set off boldly on a new course.

clue.text: Concert with one playing portable instrument

parts.note: concert means agreement, as in acting in concert, an accord
I is the Roman numeral for one
a show that is on is playing

explanation.surface: A concert in which someone performs on a carried instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' is agreement here, not a musical event.
explanation.definitionFit: An accordion is a bellows-driven keyboard instrument carried on the body.

clue.text: Jade acquired out of wages

definitions.meaning: a jade is a worn-out old horse
money obtained as pay, slang for a salary

explanation.definitionFit: An old nag is a screw in horse slang, and screw is old slang for wages or salary.

clue.text: One is glad it can be produced as a stimulant

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased it can be made into a pep pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be produced' rearranges I + IS + GLAD + IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis, from foxglove, is a drug that stimulates the heart.

clue.text: As one's clothes probably will, if one is this

definitions.text: As one's clothes probably will, if one is this

parts.words: As one's clothes probably will, if one is this
parts.note: a skirt with triangular inserted panels has them; a person pierced by a bull's horn suffers the same word, and the clothes are likely torn too

explanation.surface: Your clothing will probably share whatever fate befalls you.
explanation.walkthrough: Gores are tapered panels sewn into a skirt; the word also means stabbed by horns.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierced by a horn, and also fitted with tapering cloth panels.

clue.text: Southern Indian spent a million in the centre

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the middle of the phrase spent a million

explanation.surface: A man from the south of India squandered a fortune in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the centre' signals letters taken from the middle of 'spent a million'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamils are a people of Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka, in India's south.

clue.text: Leaderless United given black marks

indicators.note: without its leader, so the first letter of the word for united goes

parts.note: linked means joined, united

explanation.surface: A football team with no captain is penalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club; it means joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Inked means marked with ink, black writing on a page.

clue.text: Tumbler, perhaps, with less water in

definitions.meaning: a tumble machine that dries laundry
comparative of the adjective meaning not wet

explanation.definitionFit: A tumble dryer is a laundry appliance; dryer also means less wet.

clue.text: He never has a stand-up row

definitions.text: He never has a stand-up row

parts.words: He never has a stand-up row
parts.note: a stand-up row sounds like a shouting match, but here row means propelling a boat, which is done sitting down

explanation.surface: A calm man who never gets into heated arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower sits to row, so never rows standing.

clue.text: Breakdown Burton associated with melancholy

definitions.meaning: Robert Burton wrote The ... of Melancholy in 1621

explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy means detailed analysis, and is the first word of Burton's famous title.

clue.text: Award Duke got in the middle of dinner, say

indicators.note: the duke letter is placed inside the word for dinner

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal

explanation.surface: A duke receives an honour halfway through a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal is a decoration awarded for achievement.

clue.text: A weekly very similar to the Observer?

definitions.meaning: a British weekly magazine of politics and culture
one who watches, as a newspaper name hints

explanation.definitionFit: The Spectator is a long-running British weekly magazine, and a spectator is one who watches.
